reviews.author: Jordi Batlle Caminal

reviews.text: Revenge of the Sith is still junk.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: Ewan McGregor is just right, as always, as humble Obi-Wan Kenobi.
reviews.author: Paul Sherman

reviews.text: From design to execution, the creative Force is strong in this one.
reviews.author: Rick Bentley

reviews.text: [Lucas] built a perfect beast but left out the heart.
reviews.author: Christopher Kelly

reviews.text: George Lucas accomplishes what he set out to do.
reviews.author: Julie Washington

reviews.author: Margaret A. McGurk

reviews.text: It's all come home for a finale that moves way up in aesthetic class,
reviews.author: Jeff Simon

reviews.author: Akhil Arora

reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.author: David Walsh

reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: Sith comes back with full force.

reviews.text: Revenge of the Sith is far from a great film but it easily trumps its two predecessors.

reviews.text: Rich in cityscapes and costumes.

reviews.text: By golly, he did it!

reviews.text: All good things must come to an end and creator George Lucas ends his series on a pretty high note.

reviews.text: A fitting conclusion to a landmark franchise.

reviews.text: Easily the best of the prequels...

reviews.text: Well done, George. Well done.

reviews.text: All in all, this reviewer was satisfied with Star Wars III.

reviews.text: One leaves the theater with a 30-year sense of closure and satisfaction

reviews.text: We always knew it would end like this, but sheesh!

reviews.text: This is downright brilliant filmmaking, an awesome spectacle that manages to balance thrills and emotion with a steady hand.

reviews.text: If you've seen the others, you'll want to see this one. Let's face it -- there's no turning back.

reviews.text: Anakin switches teams and the force avoids becoming farce in Lucas' swan-song.

reviews.text: Like the most heavily-effects-budgeted shoulder shrug in history.

reviews.text: Redeems some of the luster lost from the previous two installments.

reviews.text: A glorious, perversely satisfying conclusion to a labor of love ... and a grand entertainment in its own right.

reviews.text: It turns out I'm still afraid of the Dark Side.

reviews.text: Be still our little saber-loving hearts! It's here...

reviews.text: I got frustrated with the high cheesy factor (disappointed in the acting I was), but I never got bored.
reviews.author: Cherryl Dawson and Leigh Ann Palone

reviews.text: Star Wars: Episode III - Revenge of the Sith is the movie we've been waiting for, the movie that should have been made all along.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: For once, the words 'A long time ago in a galaxy far, far away' seem ironic, and it's hard to watch what follows without drawing comparisons to our own political landscape.
reviews.author: John Beifuss

reviews.text: Limbs are lost, people die, destruction is widespread, and evil reigns... all this violence is courtesy a mere PG-13 rating (thanks, MPAA!)
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: Got Wood? Christensen's stiff acting almost sink this digital ship. The last hour is absolutely brilliant.
reviews.author: Michelle Alexandria

reviews.text: This one is definitely the best of the three. Fear not, fans. Lucas came through in the clutch.
reviews.author: Paul Salfen

reviews.text: It's meatier and more daring than [the first two prequels], and earns its place alongside the original Star Wars and The Empire Strikes Back.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: Lucas' attempted apolitical veneer only underlines the point: wars are political, even in movies.
reviews.author: Cynthia Fuchs

reviews.text: Too bad George Lucas was trying to write a tragedy and not a farce.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Bruner

reviews.text: While it does carry some of the flaws of the first two episodes, it thankfully lives up to its promise to be the darkest film in the series.
reviews.author: Collin Souter

reviews.text: Lucas should be barred from touching a typewriter, but, based on his work here, I'd like to see him encouraged to shoot as many fight scenes as possible.
reviews.author: Jeremy C. Fox

reviews.text: An ideal, convincing finale for this franchise.
reviews.author: David Keyes

reviews.text: Lucas' vision has matured, along with his digital special-effects tools. Lucky for us that the Force was often with him on this one.
reviews.author: Susan Tavernetti

reviews.text: ...falls down in the one area that it can't afford to - making us feel something at the moment Anakin goes to the Dark Side.
reviews.author: Andy Klein

reviews.text: This is a solid, thoroughly entertaining conclusion to a classic story.
reviews.author: Bob Grimm

reviews.text: Almost exactly what it needs to be, a powerful middle film to end one trilogy and presage another.
reviews.author: Eric D. Snider

reviews.text: A slam-bang summer blockbuster. Completes, deepens, and enriches the series beyond the pop-cultural phenomenon it has long-since made for itself.
reviews.author: Dustin Putman

reviews.text: Acquits the recent stinkiness of the series pretty well. I know, high praise indeed. But consider this - I knew what was going to happen, and I still cared.
reviews.author: Karina Montgomery

reviews.text: Beautifully choreographed, loud, furious and rib-shaking donnybrooks that are weaved of the long-gestating daydreams of fans.
reviews.author: Phil Villarreal

reviews.text: Remarkably, Lucas solicits even worse performances than in pictures past; the Mace Windu-Palpatine confrontation ranks amongst the worst acted scenes I've ever seen.
reviews.author: Todd Gilchrist

reviews.text: The only disappointment - Natalie Portman does not wear the Princess Leia gold bikini.
reviews.author: Willie Waffle

reviews.text: Revenge of the Sith is so good, it almost redeems Episode I... Almost.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: Not only a perfect bridge to the original trilogy but will draw favorable comparisons to the fabled excellence of The Empire Strikes Back.
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: George Lucas is much more interested in the reflection of some planet's third moon on a window than in the other reasons people go to movies, like acting and script.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: The film is pretty much wall-to-wall action, with little of the filibusters about trade unions that made Phantom Menace and Clones so irritating.
reviews.author: Jon Niccum

reviews.text: Nostalgie et gravit aidant, La Revanche des Sith offre certainement quelques squences d'anthologie et mme certains moments d'motion palpable.
reviews.author: Nicolas Lacroix

reviews.text: Just when you thought it was safe to ridicule everything Star Wars, Lucas returns from his flirtation with the Dark Side by crafting a terrific caper to his monumental series.
reviews.author: Lisa Kennedy

reviews.text: A film that never wields the dramatic impact its plot should demand, and never realises the emotional potential at its dark heart.
reviews.author: Peter Watts

reviews.text: Like the other two so-called 'prequels', this one still doesn't feel like a Star Wars movie . . .
reviews.author: James O'Ehley

reviews.text: A dark, dramatic, action-packed climax to the trilogy of prequels that's almost good enough to make you forgive The Phantom Menace. Almost.
reviews.author: Matthew Turner

reviews.text: At its best, Revenge of the Sith reaches that plateau where pop is art.
reviews.author: Michael Sragow

reviews.text: If only this had gotten out of the starting gate a little quicker, it would be an unqualified success.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: Episode III suffers from some of the same shortcomings... that its two recent predecessors did, only this time... far less...
reviews.author: Eric Melin

reviews.text: While Lord Lucas has failed to solve the problems that he has demonstrated throughout the sextet, he also has commandingly summited the zenith of what he is good at.
reviews.author: Annlee Ellingson

reviews.text: Revenge of the Sith might be tolerable if it weren't designed to be taken seriously.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: Otherwise known as I Was a Teenage Darth Vader, Star Wars III is dull, puerile and underwritten, not that it will matter to its lemming-like legion of fans.
reviews.author: Thomas Delapa

reviews.text: For fans it will be nirvana, and for everyone else a welcome relief.
reviews.author: Geoff Pevere

reviews.text: 'Triumphant' is the word I'd use for Sith, particularly for its superb light-saber battles, which rediscover the sheer joy and physicality missing in Star Wars since Han Solo's heyday.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: Revenge of the Sith is a brilliant consummation to a promise made a long time ago, far, far away, in a galaxy called 1977.
reviews.author: Stephen Hunter

reviews.text: Revenge of the Sith, though, stands apart from its inert, tech-obsessed predecessors. It feels, at last, like the work of a man with a story to tell.
reviews.author: Gary Thompson

reviews.text: Watching Revenge of the Sith, it's hard not to wonder if Lucas even knows how good a movie he almost made.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: The darkest, most operatic, and technologically richest Star Wars movie to date, Sith is grim, stirring entertainment and a nearly complete vindication.
reviews.author: Shawn Levy

reviews.text: The movie grabs us from its heart-pounding opening sequence and pulls us inexorably along its trajectory with the grip of the last gruesome act of a Greek tragedy.
reviews.author: William Arnold

reviews.text: Compared to the dog-fight in Star Wars this is like playing Halo instead of Pac Man.
reviews.author: Louis B. Hobson

reviews.text: George Lucas had lost his way for many years, gone to filmmaking's dark side. But now he's mustered up completely unexpected reserve for a last-minute redemption.
reviews.author: Mark Rahner

reviews.text: Though flawed, Episode III never betrays the Star Wars legacy.
reviews.author: Carla Meyer

reviews.text: Even if this movie is short of perfection, it makes Star Wars complete.
reviews.author: Bruce Kirkland

reviews.text: Ultimately, Revenge of the Sith resonates with surprising emotional power and an undeniable sense of finality.
reviews.author: Jack Garner

reviews.text: The finale feels less the inevitable conclusion of some great saga than the predictable mooing of a reliable cash cow.
reviews.author: Duane Dudek

reviews.text: For all its doom and gloom, Revenge of the Sith turns out to have a happy after all, giving Star Wars the send-off it deserves.
reviews.author: Rene Rodriguez

reviews.text: More than a first-rate wrap-up job, it stands on its own as a dazzling piece of showmanship.
reviews.author: Philip Wuntch

reviews.text: Revenge of the Sith completes the big picture and will undoubtedly find favor with a majority of fans. But it isn't a very good movie.
reviews.author: Robert W. Butler

reviews.text: Revenge of the Sith is more of the same: wildly flamboyant effects serving weak characters, bad acting and obtuse plotting.
reviews.author: Bruce Westbrook

reviews.text: Man: 'You're so beautiful.' Woman: 'It's only because I'm so in love.' Man: 'No, it's because I'm so in love with you.' Me: 'Man oh man.'
reviews.author: Rick Groen

reviews.text: George Lucas makes it easy to experience Star Wars: Episode III -- Revenge of the Sith as a rush of deliverance -- even if the movie itself doesn't fully deliver.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: Restore your faith in the Force, this will.
reviews.author: E! Staff

reviews.text: George Lucas finally achieves the sense of epic narrative weight his fans have always claimed for him.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: Lucas ha cumplido la profeca: ha trado el equilibrio a la Fuerza.
reviews.author: Alex Ramirez

reviews.text: Call it the saga's 'Darth nadir.' Lucas's greatest success in Sith is this: We can't help but sympathize with Anakin as he surrenders to the Dark Side.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Overstreet

reviews.text: I'm still not totally convinced that this is the result of good filmmaking, so much as it simply makes viewers nostalgic for the original trilogy.
reviews.author: Jon Popick

reviews.text: It's all about seeing the story lines of the sloppy prequels finally tie together with the original films. [F]ans will enjoy [watching] everything fall neatly into place.
reviews.author: Daniel M. Kimmel

reviews.text: It's all kind of like comfort food as Episode 3 finally brings you back 'to a galaxy far, far away' that we first met nearly three decades ago.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: ...writer/director George Lucas has been promising a darker film and Hayden Christensen's critical vindication. He delivers on the first promise.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: A satisfying finale... a happy payoff for fans who found Phantom Menace and the first half of Attack of the Clones to be plodding exposition.
reviews.author: James Sanford

reviews.text: Technically magnificent but dramatically inert, it's a lumberingly predictable finale to the space saga that peaked in 1980 and has been going downhill ever since.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: A great film in spite of itself.
reviews.author: Steven Snyder

reviews.text: The good George Lucas usually wins out, even if the story focuses on the Dark Side of the Force.
reviews.author: Dan Lybarger

reviews.text: Precisely what this passionate SW geek wanted: a bit less soapy dialogue, a lot more action, and a stunningly strong infusion of drama, emotion, and tragedy.
reviews.author: Scott Weinberg

reviews.text: I cried for two reasons. First, because, after nearly 30 years, it's finished. Yes, the series will be out in 3-D. But this is the finale of what George Lucas began in 1977.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: Lacking in dramatic punch, animated only by mind-numbing action sequences and endless light-saber fights.
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: What a shock when George Lucas finds his footing and the saga once again takes hold.
reviews.author: David Edelstein

reviews.text: It provides fun and closure, wrapping up the saga's many narrative strings in an entertaining finale.
reviews.author: Jeff Strickler

reviews.text: Despite all of its impressive slam-bang, almost wall-to-wall action and awe-inspiring special effects, Episode III, though head and shoulders above the other prequels, is crippled by poor scripting and logic.
reviews.author: John Paul Powell

reviews.text: Same logo. Same starry-night spacescape. Same music. Same crawl. Same everything. Only different. And so much better.
reviews.author: Eleanor Ringel Cater

reviews.text: Revenge of the Sith is both unspeakably brilliant and kind of OK, depending on where you're coming from.
reviews.author: Phoebe Flowers

reviews.text: An engaging sense of closure to a tale that has captivated more than one generation, and one that has made cinematic history
reviews.author: Leslie Katz

reviews.text: [T]here is a haunting, disconcerting bittersweetness to the film that is impossible to shake. It's a particularly GenX response, I suspect...
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: We are all preprogrammed in one way or another to want Episode III -- Revenge of the Sith to climax in the way it does. All George had to do was not screw that up. He didn't.
reviews.author: Bob Strauss

reviews.text: Heretical though it sounds, [Sith] may come closest of all the films to achieving the balance between gee-whiz sci-fi spectacle and mythic resonance to which Lucas aspired.
reviews.author: Maitland McDonagh

reviews.text: For many, the Sith finale will redeem all three prequels. Others will wonder why Lucas wasted so many dollars, years and pixels on a story that could have been told in one film, or better yet, not at all.
reviews.author: Lisa Rose

reviews.text: Lucas still can't write. His dialogue crashes and burns like an X-wing zapped out of the sky by a star destroyer.
reviews.author: Steven Rea

reviews.text: Star Wars, for better or worse, was the genuine article. How then can there not be a relevance, and a resonance, in saying goodbye?
reviews.author: Mary F. Pols

reviews.text: To say that Revenge of the Sith is a vast improvement is not extravagant praise -- but neither is it any kind of putdown.
reviews.author: Terry Lawson

reviews.text: All those who wondered whether writer-director George Lucas was going to end his sci-fi career in a downward tailspin can rest easy.
reviews.author: Tom Long

reviews.text: My favorite of the three most recent Star Wars movies, Revenge of the Sith mixes all of the best elements from its predecessors.
reviews.author: JoBlo

reviews.text: Sith takes a while to sink in, but once you get used to its rhythm, it provides the most satisfying Star Wars adventure of the last 20 years.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: While Sith is mostly enjoyable, the best part about it is that we are finally done with the journey.
reviews.author: Danny Minton

reviews.text: Ewan McGregor deserves special mention for carrying much of the film on his shoulders as Obi-Wan, genuinely getting across his crushing disappointment at mentoring Skywalker, who eventually turns to the dark side.
reviews.author: Christopher Null

reviews.text: Revenge of the Sith is the most energetic of the prequels, the only one at all worth watching. But that doesn't mean it is without the weaknesses that scuttled its pair of predecessors.
reviews.author: Kenneth Turan

reviews.text: It's the darkest of the six-film opus, but it just may be the best of the lot.
reviews.author: Claudia Puig

reviews.text: Though it starts slowly, it lumbers toward greatness in the last third and restores [Lucas] briefly to the top of his class.
reviews.author: Lawrence Toppman

reviews.text: Revenge of the Sith works because it has somewhere to go.
reviews.author: Bill Muller

reviews.text: Episode III is the ultimate lead-in to the original 1977 version and perhaps the series’ most revealing, wherein Anakin Skywalker finally succumbs to the dark side and transforms himself into the deathly malicious Darth Vader.
reviews.author: Jeanne Aufmuth

reviews.text: The Jedi faithful deserve far better than this.
reviews.author: Sean McBride

reviews.text: As he brings his beginning to an end, George Lucas finally produces a second-generation Star Wars adventure worthy of the originals.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Westhoff

reviews.text: I think it's the best one since The Empire Strikes Back.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Crippled as he is by the decisions of the first two films, Lucas manages to invest the final chapter of his space opera with the grand operatic spirit of the original trilogy.
reviews.author: Steven D. Greydanus

reviews.text: ...the dialogue is astonishingly feeble, the acting unforgivably wooden.
reviews.author: Jami Bernard

reviews.text: The scariest, most exciting, most visually prodigious of the sextet, with action sequences that explode off the screen, characters who finally awaken your sentiments.
reviews.author: Michael Wilmington

reviews.text: George Lucas has achieved what few artists do; he has created and populated a world of his own.
reviews.author: Roger Ebert

reviews.text: ... the visually stunning Sith is also the fastest-paced and most accessible.
reviews.author: Lou Lumenick

reviews.text: All those Star Wars geeks, who've been waiting for weeks outside movie theaters with their Yoda sleeping bags and their homemade lightsabers, finally have a film that's worthy of their perseverance.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: Even with its pulpy excesses showing, Revenge of the Sith has a grandiose melancholy that will especially haunt those who have grown up revering the Skywalker chronicles. The rest of the audience may well be on its own.
reviews.author: Gene Seymour

reviews.text: Lucas' pioneering work in computer-generated special effects has often gotten the better of him, but this time the action and the visual effects are splendid.
reviews.author: Bruce Newman

reviews.text: So much here is guaranteed to cause either offense or pain.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: Star Wars: Episode III - Revenge of the Sith ... is without doubt the best of the three most recent films. That's not exactly high praise...
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: This is by far the best film in the more recent trilogy, and also the best of the four episodes Mr. Lucas has directed.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: Revenge Of The Sith is brilliant. It's as if it took Lucas two goes to get comfortable in the director's chair and can now actually apply a bit of style to the proceedings.
reviews.author: Adrian MacKinder

reviews.text: Anakin's defection from Jediism to Sithdom should provide the film's backbone, but neither the script nor Christensen delivers the needed nuance.
reviews.author: Ed Halter

reviews.text: Oh my... it's neither spongeworthy nor Vader-riffic.
reviews.author: John Venable

reviews.text: Once the cogs are set in motion for the creation of Vader, & the Clone Wars start getting bloody, Sith commences to cook in a way that no movie has since Empire.
reviews.author: Glenn Kenny

reviews.text: Color me disappointed -- and I say this as a huge Star Wars fan. Its murky plotting and its long, video game battles left me cold and bored.
reviews.author: Steve Rhodes

reviews.text: Despite these deep scars, the film is visually gorgeous, a work of art, never dull, and about the biggest thing to happen on screen this year.
reviews.author: Ross Anthony

reviews.text: Let the projectionist raise the audio above a whisper, and your enjoyment of the free-flowing spectacle will be diluted by some of the worst acting and writing known to mainstream film -- and that's by George Lucas' meager standards.
reviews.author: Steve Schneider

reviews.text: Drink the Kool-Aid. Wear blinders. Cover your ears. Because that's the only way you can totally enjoy Revenge of the Sith.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: The more casual fan may be left feeling like Revenge of the Sith scores a technical knockout rather than the real thing.
reviews.author: Brent Simon

reviews.text: As it morphs to connect with Episode IV, Lucas manages to add new resonance to the overall saga.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Revenge of the Sith is not the "masterpiece" some make it out to be. It is, simply, a far more worthy installment than we've recently been fed.
reviews.author: Glen Oliver

reviews.text: Thank the movie gods this one is better than the two previous Star Wars films.
reviews.author: Rebecca Murray

reviews.text: An exhilarating, inexorably dark, somewhat distressing rollercoaster ride of fun ... the film Star Wars fans have been waiting for.
reviews.author: Caffeinated Clint

reviews.text: May be the fourth best film in the series. It's still a tossup with Ewok Adventure, but I haven't seen that in a while so it may not hold up as well.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: It may well be the best of all six Star Wars movies.
reviews.author: Rob Blackwelder

reviews.text: At last ... Lucas brings forth the long-awaited, well-earned kick-*** conclusion to the latest Star Wars trilogy. Fans will cheer!
reviews.author: David Foucher

reviews.text: Revenge of the Sith was the film that should have salvaged the prequels. It doesn't.
reviews.author: Devin Faraci

reviews.text: So sound in its construction and...[its] space-operatic catharsis that even the nitpickiest fanboy will likely adopt a humbly mumbled 'All is forgiven' as a daily mantra.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: Lucas manages to turn the audience's familiarity to his advantage: like a jigsaw puzzle whose final form has always been known, the fun is in discovering how the last pieces fit.
reviews.author: David Ansen

reviews.text: Perhaps the Dark Side is stronger after all; it certainly makes the conclusion of this journey a memorable one.
reviews.author: Rob Vaux

reviews.text: Revenge Of The Sith strings a complex plot onto a framework of practically non-stop action.
reviews.author: Paul Arendt

reviews.text: Mercifully, Revenge Of The Sith is (deep sigh) light-years ahead of the turgid Menace and the undercooked Clones.
reviews.author: Colin Kennedy

reviews.text: with a sigh of relief we come to the end of a trilogy that fell criminally short of all that is could have, and by all rights, should have been
reviews.author: Andrea Chase

reviews.text: Goodbye, Star Wars, and thanks for everything. It's been a wonderful ride.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Chen

reviews.text: The transformation, when it comes, is sensational, and all the more agonising because it is never absolute
reviews.author: Louisa McLennan

reviews.text: Will be remembered as one of the greatest movies ever made. 'Classic' isn't kind enough a word for this gem. The best film to be unleashed onto the public in 25 years!
reviews.author: Alex Sandell

reviews.text: A rousing and tragic sendoff to a beloved franchise, and the best installment in the Star Wars series since 1980's The Empire Strikes Back.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Lucas pays off the most elaborate setup in film history.
reviews.author: Jurgen Fauth

reviews.text: This film finally creates a saga out of Star Wars, and that saga deserves its recognition as one of the finest ever to be delivered to cinema screens.
reviews.author: Joe Utichi

reviews.text: The impressively mounted and emotionally engaging “Episode III–Revenge of the Sith” does proud to the entire “Star Wars” saga.
reviews.author: Emanuel Levy

reviews.text: A good film, but just not the classic it could have been.
reviews.author: Edward Havens

reviews.text: If, as director Lucas has said, this is the final film in the saga, he has done himself justice by going out with a winner.
reviews.author: Michael A. Smith

reviews.text: The magic died a long time ago, see, Episode III is just the death twitch.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: I imagine that Revenge of the Sith is very much the film Lucas's fans want to see, but are some of them ready for an anti-Bush diatribe?
reviews.author: Ed Gonzalez

reviews.text: Even though Ian McDiarmid is a delicious bad guy, John Williams' music is what sets this apart from other mundane films that survive on special effects.
reviews.author: Tony Medley

reviews.text: Enthralling and triumphant, Lucas saved the best for last, completing a significant cultural phenomenon that now encompasses six films.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Finally, Lucas recaptures some of the magic!
reviews.author: Scott Nash

reviews.text: With strong performances by Ian McDiarmid, Ewan McGregor, and Yoda, it delivers much of the action and darkness that fans have been looking for. The final connection with the Classic Trilogy ultimately makes it a satisfying conclusion to the Saga.
reviews.author: Scott Chitwood

reviews.text: The final episode of George Lucas’ cinematic epic Star Wars ends the six-movie series on such a high note that one feels like yelling out, Rewind! Yes, rewind through more than 13 hours of bravery, treachery, new worlds, odd creatures and human frailty.
reviews.author: Kirk Honeycutt

reviews.text: Whatever one thought of the previous two installments, this dynamic picture irons out most of the problems, and emerges as the best in the overall series since The Empire Strikes Back.
reviews.author: Todd McCarthy

reviews.text: An unexpectedly sweet pleasure... a dark and gripping slice of space opera, it successfully avoids the pitfalls of its predecessors.
reviews.author: Gabriel Shanks

reviews.text: Star Wars fans have finally been rewarded for their patience. George has made another masterpiece.
reviews.author: Joshua Tyler

reviews.text: We already know how this film turns out and no one at Lucasfilm has the wit to make the journey interesting.
reviews.author: Matthew De Abaitua

synopsis: It has been three years since the Clone Wars began. Jedi Master Obi-Wan Kenobi (Ewan McGregor) and Jedi Knight Anakin Skywalker (Hayden Christensen) rescue Chancellor Palpatine (Ian McDiarmid) from General Grievous, the commander of the droid armies, but Grievous escapes. Suspicions are raised within the Jedi Council concerning Chancellor Palpatine, with whom Anakin has formed a bond. Asked to spy on the chancellor, and full of bitterness toward the Jedi Council, Anakin embraces the Dark Side.
